title: Attitude Scales: Likert, Thurstone, Guttman, Semantic Differential, Stapel, Sociometry
summary: Attitude measurement; Likert scale; Thurstone's law of comparative judgment; Guttman scalogram; semantic differential (Osgood); Stapel scale; sociometry.
objectives: Describe Likert, Thurstone, Guttman, semantic differential and Stapel scales.
Explain Osgood's three factors (evaluation, potency, activity).
revision: Attitude scales: Likert (summed agree-disagree), Thurstone (paired comparisons), Guttman (cumulative), Semantic differential (bipolar adjectives, Osgood's E-P-A), Stapel (−5 to +5), Sociometry (social relations).

notes.t: A measuring instrument designed to assess a person's attitude (favourable or unfavourable evaluation) toward an object, person or issue.
Respondents indicate agreement/disagreement with statements on a symmetric agree–disagree scale (e.g., strongly agree to strongly disagree). Scores are summed across items.
A method of paired comparisons to scale attitudes. Items are ranked by the proportion of times each is preferred.
A cumulative scale where items are ordered by difficulty; endorsing a harder item implies endorsing all easier items.
Respondents rate a concept on bipolar adjective scales (e.g., good–bad, active–passive). Osgood identified three factors: evaluation, potency, activity.

i: Stapel scale: single adjective with −5 to +5 rating (no bipolar pair).
Sociometry: measures social relationships and group structure.

notes.t: UGC NET frequently asks to distinguish Likert (summed agree-disagree), semantic differential (bipolar adjectives) and Guttman (cumulative).
